title: The House Behind the Cedars
description: Published in 1900 and the classic American novel of racial passing: the story of a brother and sister who pass for white in South Carolina and of the catastrophe that follows. It is a prose fiction work of 1900 by Charles W. Chesnutt; it belongs to American Realism and the Howells Program and it is catalogued here under Sensation Novel; Novel of Development and the Growth Story.
plot_or_argument: Rena Walden, of mixed race and fair enough to pass, joins her brother John, now the white lawyer John Warwick, in the South Carolina town of Clarence and is courted by the well-born George Tryon; when he discovers her origin he abandons her, and, pursued both by the repentant Tryon and by the predatory Jeff Wain, she flees into the swamp and is carried home by her faithful friend Frank Fowler to die of brain fever.
narrative_structure: A novel of sensation in chapters, the secret withheld and revealed by stages, testimony and documents inserted into the narrative, each part closing on a cliff. A novel in chapters grouped by the stages of a life, from childhood through the education and the first disappointments to the settlement of the adult.
principal_characters: Rena Walden; John Walden (John Warwick), her brother; Molly Walden, their mother; George Tryon; Frank Fowler; Jeff Wain
literary_form: Novel; sensation novel, first issued in 1900
meter_and_prosody: Prose. Prose of sensation: the cliff-edge chapter ending, the first-person testimony and the document inserted into the narrative, the secret withheld and revealed by stages, and the vocabulary of the law, the asylum and the will. The author's characteristic manner is frame narrative that turns the oral tale against itself.

The record dates the work as composed between 1898 and 1900 and first published in 1900 and the corpus places it within American Realism and the Howells Program, it is catalogued under sensation novel; novel of development and the growth story.

title: The Colonel's Dream

narrative_structure: A novel in chapters of the industrial town, the mill, the strike and the household described in the vocabulary of the trade, the plot built on the collision of the two nations.
principal_characters: Colonel Henry French; Phil French, his son; old Peter; Laura Treadwell; Graciella Treadwell; Ben Dudley; William Fetters; Bud Johnson

The record dates the work as composed between 1904 and 1905 and first published in 1905 and the corpus places it within American Realism and the Howells Program, it is catalogued under industrial and condition-of-england novel; social inquiry and the documented survey.

title: Lyrics of Lowly Life
description: Published in 1896 with an introduction by William Dean Howells and the book that made Dunbar famous: the dialect poems of the old plantation and the standard English lyrics of love, grief and race. It is a verse work of 1896 by Paul Laurence Dunbar; it belongs to Mark Twain and the Vernacular Performance and it is catalogued here under Dialect Poem and Vernacular Performance; Pastoral Elegy and the Mourning Sequence and the record grades it as major canon.

narrative_structure: A collection of poems written to be performed, each a separate monologue or song in the spoken dialect. An elegiac sequence: the stanzas repeat the mourning pattern, and the poem moves from the news of the death, through the lament and the questioning, to the consolation or the refusal of consolation.
literary_form: Poetry collection (with an introduction by William Dean Howells)
meter_and_prosody: Verse. Verse in dialect and vernacular: the spelling carries the pronunciation, the stanza is song-like and often rhymed in ballad measure, and the poem is written to be spoken or performed aloud. The work is a collection of separate pieces in the author's or editor's order. The author's characteristic manner is dialect verse in the plantation tradition, handled with real lyric skill.

title: 'We Wear the Mask'
description: Written in 1895 and published in Majors and Minors and then in Lyrics of Lowly Life: the central American poem of the mask, in which the black speaker addresses a deceitful world. It is a verse work of 1896 by Paul Laurence Dunbar; it belongs to Mark Twain and the Vernacular Performance and it is catalogued here under Dramatic Monologue and Masked Lyric; Dialect Poem and Vernacular Performance and the record grades it as major canon.
plot_or_argument: The speaker describes the mask that 'grins and lies' and hides the cheeks and eyes of a people who smile while their torn hearts bleed, and asks Christ only that the world be not allowed to see beyond the mask.
narrative_structure: A sequence of monologues, each spoken by a different character in a different scene, with the silent listener implied in every line. A collection of poems written to be performed, each a separate monologue or song in the spoken dialect.
literary_form: Lyric poem (in Majors and Minors, 1895; Lyrics of Lowly Life, 1896)
meter_and_prosody: Three five-line stanzas of iambic tetrameter and trimeter, rhymed aabba, with a refrain.
historical_context: The 1890s: the Jim Crow South, the politics of accommodation, and the double consciousness of the black American. The record dates the work as composed in 1895 and first published in 1896 and the corpus places it within Mark Twain and the Vernacular Performance; The Dramatic Monologue and the Masked Voice, it is catalogued under dramatic monologue and masked lyric; dialect poem and vernacular performance.

title: The Sport of the Gods
description: Published in 1902 and Dunbar's finest novel: the destruction of a respectable black family by a false accusation, and their migration to New York. It is a prose fiction work of 1902 by Paul Laurence Dunbar; it belongs to American Naturalism and the Determinist Tragedy and it is catalogued here under Naturalist and Determinist Novel; Industrial and Condition-of-England Novel.

A novel in chapters of the industrial town, the mill, the strike and the household described in the vocabulary of the trade, the plot built on the collision of the two nations.

An elegiac sequence: the stanzas repeat the mourning pattern, and the poem moves from the news of the death, through the lament and the questioning, to the consolation or the refusal of consolation.

title: The Complete Poems of Paul Laurence Dunbar
alternative_titles: Complete Poems of Paul Laurence Dunbar
description: Published in 1913 after his death and the standard collection of Dunbar's verse: the dialect poems, the standard English lyrics and the late poems of love and death. plot_or_argument: The volume gathers the four major collections and the uncollected poems, and shows the full range of Dunbar's work — the plantation dialect that made him famous, the lyrics of 'The Debt', 'Slow through the Dark' and 'The Haunted Oak', and the poems of his last illness.
narrative_structure: A collection of poems written to be performed, each a separate monologue or song in the spoken dialect. title: Little Women
description: Published in two parts in 1868 and 1869 and the most beloved American family novel: the lives of the four March sisters from adolescence to marriage. title: Hospital Sketches
description: Published in 1863 and based on Alcott's service as a nurse at the Union Hotel Hospital in Georgetown: the first great American book of the Civil War from a woman's point of view. It is a prose work of 1863 by Louisa May Alcott; it belongs to American Realism and the Howells Program and it is catalogued here under War Narrative of the Common Soldier; Review Essay and Quarterly Argument.
plot_or_argument: Tribulation Periwinkle, the narrator, travels to Washington, takes up her duties among the wounded, and records the deaths, the jokes and the ordinariness of the hospital, ending with her own illness and return home.
narrative_structure: A first-person narrative of service, organised by the stages of the campaign and told in the plain idiom of the ranks. An essay in sections, the argument stated, the evidence quoted, the objection answered and the judgement delivered, in the compass of the quarterly review.
literary_form: Collection of letters (first published in the Commonwealth, 1863)
meter_and_prosody: Prose. Prose of the common soldier: the plain first-person account, the exact vocabulary of the trench, the ration, the march and the casualty, and the understatement that carries the horror. title: Work: A Story of Experience

title: Behind a Mask; or, A Woman's Power

It is a prose fiction work of 1866 by Louisa May Alcott; it belongs to Sensation Fiction and the Serial Plot and it is catalogued here under Sensation Novel.

narrative_structure: A novel of sensation in chapters, the secret withheld and revealed by stages, testimony and documents inserted into the narrative, each part closing on a cliff.

title: 'Life in the Iron-Mills'

title: Margret Howth: A Story of To-Day
description: Published in 1862 and the first American novel of the industrial working woman: the story of a mill town and of the woman who keeps her family alive by her labour.
